\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{પેન્શન} (penśan)}{પેન્શન (penśan)}]{\gu{પેન્શન} (penśan) — a pension}

\label{lesson:GU-C427-pensan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to multiply, then the Gujarati for to increase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{પેન્શન}}
\textbf{\gu{પેન્શન}} — \emph{penśan} — \textquotedblleft{}a pension\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{નિવૃત્ત} \gu{થયા} \gu{પછી} \gu{દાદાને} \gu{પેન્શન} \gu{મળે} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nivṛtt thayā pachī dādāne penśan maḷe che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Since he retired, grandfather has received a pension.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{પેન્શન}} (\emph{penśan}) is borrowed from English \emph{pension}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{penśan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{penśan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nivṛtt thayā pachī dādāne penśan maḷe che.} — Since he retired, grandfather has received a pension.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to multiply, then the Gujarati for to increase, then say \emph{penśan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{પેન્શન} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A pension\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{રોકાણ} (rokāṇ)}{રોકાણ (rokāṇ)}]{\gu{રોકાણ} (rokāṇ) — an investment}

\label{lesson:GU-C427-rokan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to increase, then the Gujarati for a pension.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{રોકાણ}}
\textbf{\gu{રોકાણ}} — \emph{rokāṇ} — \textquotedblleft{}an investment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તેણે} \gu{બચતનું} \gu{રોકાણ} \gu{બેંકમાં} \gu{કર્યું}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{teṇe bacatnũ rokāṇ beṅkmā̃ karyũ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She invested her savings in the bank.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{રોકાણ}} (\emph{rokāṇ}) is built on \gu{રોકવું}, to stop, to hold back, which goes back to \emph{*rōkk}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 10827): money held back and put to work.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rokāṇ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rokāṇ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{teṇe bacatnũ rokāṇ beṅkmā̃ karyũ.} — She invested her savings in the bank.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for to increase, then the Gujarati for a pension, then say \emph{rokāṇ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{રોકાણ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An investment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{થાપણ} (thāpaṇ)}{થાપણ (thāpaṇ)}]{\gu{થાપણ} (thāpaṇ) — a deposit (of money); something held in trust}

\label{lesson:GU-C427-thapan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a pension, then the Gujarati for an investment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{થાપણ}}
\textbf{\gu{થાપણ}} — \emph{thāpaṇ} — \textquotedblleft{}a deposit (of money); something held in trust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મારી} \gu{થાપણ} \gu{પર} \gu{બેંક} \gu{વ્યાજ} \gu{આપે} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mārī thāpaṇ par beṅk vyāj āpe che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bank pays interest on my deposit.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{થાપણ}} (\emph{thāpaṇ}) seems to go back to Sanskrit \emph{sthāpana}, \textquotedblleft{}setting down, placing\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): money set down with someone to keep.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{thāpaṇ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mārī thāpaṇ par beṅk vyāj āpe che.} — The bank pays interest on my deposit.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a pension, then the Gujarati for an investment, then say \emph{thāpaṇ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{મુદત} (mudat)}{મુદત (mudat)}]{\gu{મુદત} (mudat) — a fixed term; a period (of time)}

\label{lesson:GU-C427-mudat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for an investment, then the Gujarati for a deposit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{મુદત}}
\textbf{\gu{મુદત}} — \emph{mudat} — \textquotedblleft{}a fixed term; a period (of time)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{આ} \gu{થાપણની} \gu{મુદત} \gu{પાંચ} \gu{વરસની} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā thāpaṇnī mudat pā̃c varasnī che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The term of this deposit is five years.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{મુદત}} (\emph{mudat}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{mudda}, \textquotedblleft{}a space of time\textquotedblright{}, which came through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mudat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mudat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā thāpaṇnī mudat pā̃c varasnī che.} — The term of this deposit is five years.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for an investment, then the Gujarati for a deposit, then say \emph{mudat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{મુદત} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fixed term; a period (of time)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ફાળવવું} (phāḷavvũ)}{ફાળવવું (phāḷavvũ)}]{\gu{ફાળવવું} (phāḷavvũ) — to set aside (money); to allot}

\label{lesson:GU-C427-phalavvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a deposit, then the Gujarati for a fixed term.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ફાળવવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ફાળવવું}} — \emph{phāḷavvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to set aside (money); to allot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મેં} \gu{પગારમાંથી} \gu{બચત} \gu{માટે} \gu{પૈસા} \gu{ફાળવ્યા}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mẽ pagārmā̃thī bacat māṭe paisā phāḷavyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I set aside money from my salary for savings.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{પૈસા} \gu{ફાળવ્યા}, \emph{teṇe paisā phāḷavyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ફાળવવું}} (\emph{phāḷavvũ}) is built on \gu{ફાળો}, a share, which goes back to \emph{*phāla}, a form CDIAL reconstructs and lists for the Gujarati word (CDIAL 9073): to give each thing its share.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phāḷavvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phāḷavvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mẽ pagārmā̃thī bacat māṭe paisā phāḷavyā.} — I set aside money from my salary for savings.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a deposit, then the Gujarati for a fixed term, then say \emph{phāḷavvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ફાળવવું} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To set aside (money); to allot\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
